what_its_for: This medicine is used to treat certain types of acute myeloid leukemia (AML), which is a cancer of the blood and bone marrow. It is specifically used for adults with newly diagnosed AML that is related to prior cancer therapy or has certain genetic changes (myelodysplasia-related changes). The two chemotherapy medicines inside this drug are packaged together in tiny fat-like bubbles called liposomes, which help deliver them directly to cancer cells.
how_to_take: This medicine is given to you by a nurse or doctor through an intravenous (IV) line directly into your vein. You will NOT give this medicine to yourself at home. Each infusion takes about 90 minutes. You will receive this treatment in a hospital or clinic setting, and your healthcare team will closely monitor you during and after each infusion. Do NOT receive this drug if it looks cloudy, has particles, or is discolored — always let your nurse check the bag before it is given to you.
dosing: Your doctor will calculate your dose based on your body size (height and weight). The typical treatment schedule has two phases: (1) INDUCTION — you receive the drug on Days 1, 3, and 5 of a treatment cycle (up to 2 induction cycles may be given depending on your response); (2) CONSOLIDATION — if your leukemia responds, you may receive additional doses on Days 1 and 3 of up to 2 more cycles. Your doctor will decide how many cycles you need based on your response, lab results, and how well you tolerate treatment. Never try to adjust your own dose.
missed_dose: Because this medicine is given by healthcare professionals in a clinic or hospital, a missed dose will be managed by your medical team. If you cannot keep your scheduled appointment, call your doctor or treatment center as soon as possible to reschedule. Do not skip or delay treatments without talking to your doctor first, as this may affect how well the medicine works.
storage: You do not store this medicine at home. It is stored and prepared by pharmacy staff in the hospital or clinic. For your information: the unopened vials are kept refrigerated between 36°F and 46°F (2°C to 8°C). Once mixed (diluted), the prepared solution must be used within 4 hours if kept at room temperature, or within 24 hours if refrigerated. It should never be frozen.
what_to_avoid: - Do NOT receive live vaccines (such as the nasal flu spray, shingles live vaccine, or yellow fever vaccine) while on this treatment and for some time after, without talking to your doctor first. - Avoid close contact with people who are sick or have infections, as this medicine lowers your immune system. - Avoid crowds and wash your hands frequently. - Avoid activities that could cause cuts or bruising since this medicine can lower your platelet count and make bleeding more likely. - Women of childbearing age should use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 6 months after the last dose. Men with female partners who can become pregnant should also use contraception during treatment and for at least 3 months after. - Do not breastfeed while receiving this medicine and for at least 2 weeks after the final dose. - Discuss all prescription medicines, over-the-counter drugs, vitamins, and herbal supplements with your doctor before starting treatment, as some medicines may interact.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor or go to the emergency room right away if you experience any of the following: - Fever of 100.4°F (38°C) or higher, chills, or signs of infection (this is a medical emergency during chemotherapy) - Unusual bleeding or bruising, or blood in your urine or stool - Severe shortness of breath, sudden weight gain, or swelling of the legs or ankles (signs of heart or fluid problems) - Chest pain or irregular heartbeat - Severe nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea that will not stop - Mouth sores that are very painful or preventing you from eating - Yellowing of your skin or eyes (jaundice) - Dark or tea-colored urine - Signs of an infusion reaction during or after the IV: rash, hives, difficulty breathing, dizziness, or feeling faint - Extreme tiredness or weakness - Any new or unusual symptoms that concern you. Your healthcare team will monitor you with regular blood tests and heart tests (echocardiogram or MUGA scan) throughout your treatment.
when_it_works: This medicine starts working right away at the cellular level, but it may take days to weeks before your doctor can confirm how well it is working. Your doctor will check your bone marrow and blood counts after each induction cycle (usually around Day 14 and again around Day 28) to see how your leukemia is responding. Some patients may see signs of remission (cancer going away) after the first cycle, while others may need a second cycle. It is important to complete your treatment as scheduled even if you do not feel immediate changes. Be patient and keep all of your follow-up appointments.
special_populations: PREGNANCY: This medicine can harm an unborn baby. Do not become pregnant while receiving this drug. Tell your doctor immediately if you become pregnant. BREASTFEEDING: Do not breastfeed during treatment or for at least 2 weeks after the last dose. FERTILITY: This medicine may affect fertility (ability to have children) in both men and women. Talk to your doctor about fertility preservation options before starting treatment. OLDER ADULTS (65 years and older): This medicine has been used in older adults. Your doctor will monitor you closely for side effects such as heart problems, infections, and bleeding. KIDNEY OR LIVER PROBLEMS: Your doctor will review your kidney and liver function before and during treatment, as these conditions may affect how the medicine is processed in your body. HEART DISEASE: Because this medicine contains daunorubicin, it can affect heart function. Tell your doctor about any history of heart disease. You will have heart function tests before and during treatment.
